review:
1100 hours later and I’m still playing

I wanted BeamNG for a couple of years before I finally bought it and it was honestly worth the wait

The physics are insane Every car feels different and the damage suspension and handling are on another level You can spend hours just driving around testing cars or messing with different builds

The new update made the game even better especially for taking screenshots The lighting and graphics look amazing now and it really helps me make more realistic car shots which is one of my favorite things to do in this game

The modding community is also one of the best parts There are so many great cars maps and other mods that there’s always something new to try

I also like that the developers actually care about the game They keep improving it adding new content fixing things and making it better instead of leaving it behind

If you’re thinking about buying BeamNG just do it I definitely got my money’s worth and I can easily see myself putting another 1100 hours into this game

I am currently a traffic crash investigator for a Sheriff's Department in the US. Not only is this "game" fun, it has the potential to be a great tool in the field of traffic crash reconstruction. The physics engine hands down is VERY close to the real thing. Part of my job consists of taking real world crash data, reconstructing and mathematically remodeling crash and vehicle dynamics. That said, not only is this game (simulator really) extremely fun, it has the potential down the road to aid law enforcement in the reconstruction of fatal crashes. Similar programs that take raw physics data and convert them to 3D renderings such as this one can go for upwards of $50,000. Although Beamng.drive is not to the level of forensic software, it could be with some tweaking and insight.

I highly recommend this title and I can't wait to see what future updates hold. There are some bugs, but this isn't the full game and is to be expected.

To the developers ---- consider speaking with a consulting firm in crash reconstruction to get the correct formulas, equations, etc, and you could possibly license a professional version, which could spell big money. Some type of mode to enter real world vehicles, manipulate vehicle weights, be able to place them on a road at certain angles and certain speeds etc. would be awesome. I can tell you already that the game in its current state will yield crash results in the same ballpark, very close to the real world.
this game really makes me wanna crash my car in real life and see if the physics match up

Physics-based sandbox + cars + healthy modding community.
Possibilities are endless. 
You wanna have fun? Here it is.
You wanna simulate real-life accidents? Here it is.
You wanna test the limits of your rig? Drive in ai traffic with settings on max with a bunch of mods and it'll be here.
You wanna compare the impacts of Jupiter's gravity on a pick-up truck vs. the moon's gravity? Here it is.
You wanna customize and tune your own Drift Car? Drag Car? Rally car? JATO rocket semi? All here.
You wanna create your own map to drive a Nissan GTR you got from one of the 1000's of mods? Here it is.
You wanna play with friends to see who can make it down an 'impossible to survive' hill unscathed? Here it is.
You wanna zoom past ai traffic jams on city highways? Or crash into them in slow mo? Here and here.
You wanna go off-roading, where each rock and muddy patch accurately affects your car's suspension, differential, and traction? Here it is.
You want decent force feedback on your sim wheel set-up, which in tandem with the hefty physics model gives you some of the most realistic driving feel any game has come up with? Here in spades.
You want it to be affordable, with no payed DLC or online service? Gladly here.
You wanna .drive? It's in the name dummy, if you got this far in the review you're wasting time better spent playing this game.

BeamNG is an absolute must-have for every car lover. If you want realistic driving, off-roading, racing, a soft-body damage system, car customization and tuning, or just want to sit back and relax while driving your favorite car in an open-world map with traffic, BeamNG has it all. The variety of vehicles is incredible, ranging from everyday cars to massive trucks, and if you can’t find something you like in the vanilla game, you will most likely find it as a mod. In conclusion, BeamNG is an amazing game that offers realistic physics, endless fun, and something for every type of player. It’s absolutely worth buying.

xcellent Support Service

I had a technical issue with BeamNG.drive, and the customer support team was simply outstanding. They responded quickly, professionally, and politely to all my emails, helping me resolve the problem despite my numerous requests. Not only did they solve the issue, but they did so with exceptional kindness and availability, which is rare to find. I highly recommend the game not just for its quality, but also for the amazing support team behind it.
Thank you again to the BeamNG team!

Originally, I had wrote a 2.5-page essay, explaining my review of BeamNG.drive after 2,000 hours. I later found out that Steam actually has a character limit on reviews, so I'm going to have to summarize it.

As of version 0.21, BeamNG outclasses every other game I've played (including those that aren't car games) in controller support, player control, mod support and simulation depth.
Currently, the base game lacks a main objective, shader quality and global optimizations, but it is still in development and based on its track record, it will continue to improve with every update.
I really wish I could post my entire review about the game here, but I guess the final paragraph will be good enough:

So, in conclusion, BeamNG.drive is still very much in early-access, but it has improved vastly from what it used to be, and continues to improve with every update. Almost every aspect about BeamNG.drive is much more advanced than anything else on the market, even with the odd “unfinished game” thing here and there. Because of that, and despite all of its flaws, I’d strongly recommend anyone who is into cars (and who has a PC powerful enough to run it) to give it a try. There are small things here that make it so BeamNG’s simulation is not quite perfect, but that being said, it is still the most in-depth automotive simulator that you can buy today.

There are racing games, there are driving simulators, and then there's BeamNG.drive.

Calling this game a "car crash simulator" is selling it incredibly short. The crashes are impressive, but they're only the result of what makes BeamNG so special: one of the most sophisticated soft-body physics systems ever created in a consumer game.

Unlike traditional racing games, where a vehicle is essentially a rigid object with a damage texture slapped on after an impact, every vehicle in BeamNG is built from a network of interconnected nodes and beams. Every suspension arm, chassis rail, driveshaft, and body panel reacts to forces independently. Hit a curb too hard and your steering geometry changes. Clip a guardrail and your wheel alignment is ruined. Land a jump poorly and your suspension compresses unevenly, permanently affecting how the car drives.

Nothing feels scripted.

Every crash is unique because the physics determine the outcome in real time. The angle of impact, speed, weight distribution, suspension setup, and momentum all influence what happens next. Two crashes at nearly identical speeds can produce completely different results.

The attention to detail goes far beyond destruction.

Weight transfer feels natural while cornering. Body roll changes depending on the vehicle. Tires lose grip progressively rather than instantly. Different drivetrains behave differently under acceleration. Off-roading feels genuinely mechanical instead of arcade-like, and every vehicle has its own personality because its engineering is actually modeled rather than approximated.

What amazes me most is how educational BeamNG can be.

You don't just see why a vehicle loses control—you understand it. You can feel oversteer develop because too much weight shifts rearward. You can watch suspension components fail under excessive load. You begin appreciating concepts like momentum, center of gravity, chassis rigidity, and suspension geometry simply by driving.

Then there's the variety.

Want to casually cruise scenic mountain roads? You can.

Want to rally through dirt trails? Absolutely.

Want to race AI traffic, crawl over rocks, drift, haul cargo, recreate real-world accidents, or launch buses off cliffs for science? BeamNG somehow supports all of it without ever feeling like it's forcing a particular playstyle.

The developers also deserve enormous credit.
Years after its Early Access release, BeamNG.drive continues receiving meaningful updates rather than superficial content drops. New vehicles aren't simply added—they're engineered with remarkable attention to detail, often introducing entirely new technologies, physics improvements, and gameplay systems. Maps continue to expand, career mode keeps evolving, and performance improvements make an already ambitious simulation even better.

The modding community is equally incredible. Thousands of high-quality vehicles, maps, scenarios, and utilities extend an already massive sandbox into something you can spend hundreds—or even thousands—of hours exploring.

Is it perfect? No.

The AI can still have its quirks. Career mode is still evolving. Running complex simulations with multiple vehicles requires a capable CPU, and beginners may initially find the realistic driving more demanding than traditional racing games.

But those are minor criticisms compared to what BeamNG achieves.

BeamNG.drive isn't just one of the best driving games ever made—it's one of the most technically impressive physics simulations available on PC. It rewards curiosity, experimentation, and creativity in ways that very few games can.

Whether you're an automotive enthusiast, an engineering student, a simulator fan, or someone who simply enjoys watching physics behave exactly as they should, BeamNG.drive offers an experience that no other game truly replicates.

It's not the crashes that keep people coming back.

It's the physics.

When I first downloaded this game a few years ago, I only had a gamepad and I just didn't get it. I didn't take the time to set up the controller and didn't really understand what the game is. But I love driving games (particularly rally sims - RBR, DR2.0, WRC9) and physics simulations so I spent a few hours on it and figured I'd revisit later. After quarantine started I got a wheel, so naturally tried every driving game I own with it. BeamNG.drive was by far the biggest surprise, and has quickly become one of my favorite games. Most of the cars handle as I'd expect, and I was impressed by the force feedback.

It took a couple mods to get me addicted. Pseudo Random Tour seems like a perfect mod for this game, and shows off how much content and potential there really is here. But as a rally fan, what really got me hooked was the pace notes mod (Pace Notes Core and the configuration) - Suddenly it's a rally sim, and in my opinion a really solid one. Finally, we have a game where the physics feels right, cars handle believably, and damage is realistic enough to make every risk a calculation. I don't really know how driving on tarmac compares to other games, but if you're into Dirt Rally, WRC or RBR, I'd definitely recommend checking it out. The off-road experience is exactly what I'd been wanting.

My only fear is that it could be hard to market a game like this and grow an ecosystem around it. This is a fantastic physics platform just begging to have a deeper game experience built on top of it, and I really, really hope they can create that. I'll be doing time trials in Utah until then.

Edit: I'm using a T300 RS GT with the Sparco R383 rim.

Ah, BeamNG. Probably one of the hardest games to write a review for, with the vast amount of stuff this game offers. Like driving cars? This game has cars. It also has trucks. There's also a van. And a piano. There's also a functional cannon.

 Like crashing cars?  You can do that. Whether you chuck it off a cliff, slam it into a tree, crash it into another car, or yeet it  into a destructible brick wall, you're almost always to get realistic results each and every time.

 Like driving? You can drive. Sometimes at over 300 miles per hour. You can also drive at many places, including, but not limited to: Italy, Utah, The U.S. West Coast, the U.S. East Coast, and a flat grid. You can also make your own places to drive, though its a pretty complex process. 

Not satisfied with the standard game? You can get mods, including custom vehicles such as: Dog, really-really-really tall van, big tires, and a foam block wall. There are also mods that add new places to drive to the game, such as: really long highway, ski jump designed for cars, and a couple of maps that cant really be described using text.

Worried the game wont run on your system? Alright, thats actually a reasonable thing to be worried about. This is a VERY hardware intensive game, but it can run on rather low-end devices, albeit, poorly. Chances are, if your setup is from 2014 or later, you can probably get 45+ FPS at most maps.

At the end of the day, this is a really fun vehicle sandbox game. I'd recommend it to anybody who likes cars or games with really good destruction physics.

[h2]Overall: 10/10[/h2]

BeamNG.drive isn't your average driving game. There really isn't another game out there doing what this one is doing, especially [i]how[/i] it's doing it. Rather than focusing on high-speed races or flashy stunts, BeamNG at it's core is all about physics and realism, offering a fascinating and unique experience that feels more like a driving simulator than a traditional racing game.
Easily, the biggest appeal is the advanced soft-body physics engine. This game's engine simulates every part of a vehicle in real-time and makes crashes look and feel incredibly realistic. Each impact results in dynamic deformation, with vehicles crumpling and parts flying off based on the speed and angle of the collision. Whether you’re simply driving around, performing stunts, or causing spectacular crashes, the level of detail in these interactions is actually wild, additionally so since you can adjust the game speed to be as fast or as slow as you desire. 
BeamNG's driving mechanics themselves are also pretty realistic, and it makes the game sometimes challenging but rewarding for those who appreciate true-to-life simulation. Since this game offers a wide range of vehicles from sports cars and trucks to buses and off-roaders, you're able to really feel how each vehicle handles differently, and see that their destruction is equally unique. However, despite these vanilla vehicles being fun and satisfying to watch be destroyed, the modded vehicles are definitely thing thing that really adds hours upon hours of replayability. With hundreds if not THOUSANDS of car mods online, there's endless satisfying destruction of real licensed vehicles to be observed within this amazing car physics sim.
Speaking of customization-adjacent depth though, BeamNG continues to shine in its variety of environments and the sheer amount of customization it offers both through vanilla in-game features and general mod support. You can drive through diverse maps created by both official devs and passionate modders that range from urban streets to rugged off-road trails, each with their own set of challenges. However, customization goes beyond just the visual aspects. You have the ability to tweak the physics settings, individual vehicle components, and even create your own crash tests or obstacle courses. This level of detail is perfect for anyone who loves to experiment with cars, push the boundaries of the game’s physics, or just make an absolute mess of a vehicle worthy of destruction.
Visually, this game isn’t the most stunning one out there, but it does a commendable job given the complex physics it’s running in the background. The environments are still pretty detailed, the vanilla vehicles models are actually rather pleasing to look at, and it honestly runs great. Nevertheless, I'm sure this game can be demanding on older hardware (especially when dealing with multiple vehicles or high-speed collisions) but I first picked up BeamNG when I still had a 2080 Super GPU, and most of the vanilla game can be handled decently enough on mid-range PCs. The deeper you get into modding, though, and more detailed cars, maps, etc., then you'll probably struggle to get the performance you desire without a high-end/powerful PCs, but that's not to say this game necessarily exclusive to these kind of systems by any means.

[h2]TL;DR:[/h2]

BeamNG.drive isn’t for everyone. It’s a game that thrives on experimentation and a deep appreciation for realistic physics. While the soft-body car physics can be pretty demanding on lower end PCs and it may not currently have the complete, well-structured gameplay or polished graphics of other driving games, its uniqueness and strongest features lie in its simulation of vehicle dynamics and crashes and mod support. For those who love to tinker, explore, and watch some of their favorite cars meet their untimely demise in the most realistic way possible, BeamNG.drive is a MUST-BUY!

BeamNG.drive is a successor to Rigs of Rods. The game itself is two steps ahead other games in terms of realistic vehicle simulation and its soft-body physics, so thanks to this it's unique. Driving cars is easy, just press W, but controlling them is a whole different story. Disabling automatic clutch, gearbox safety and playing on a manual gearbox using a steering wheel makes the game a lot harder to play, but that's the fun here. Tuning cars, especially with mods, is really fun and rewarding once you master it. I've never seen a game with this much car tuning capabilites, so that makes it stand out among others. Mods make the gameplay 10x better, as there are infinite possibilities to play the game. For now, there are only short scenarios and freeroam, that can get boring after some time, but a career mode is in the making since the game is in early access. The game in its current state is really fun as-is, and it will continue to expand in the future. The devs are updating and hotfixing the game frequently, so that is a big plus. Also, I hope BeamNG will get optimised more and more, because rendering and calculating physics is really CPU intensive, so playing with more than 1-2 cars will drop your framerate, especially on big maps, like West Coast USA. Overall, if you like cars you need to play this game, it's really fun once you get into it. The VR gameplay is addicting, although it can get quite buggy sometimes as using the Vulkan renderer is required

This car sim (deserving big letters: CAR SIM) reminds me of a musician fellow of mine. He plays in a clown cover band that is a sort of parody of many other famous bands. A project that is amusing but you can't take it seriously as a real band. Then, the actual guy is miles high the most talented guitarist I've ever met personally, world class, with great ideas. But he never took himself seriously enought to become a song writer or start his own band.

So, BeamNG.drive has a magnificent physical engine under the hood that becomes a face-melting experience every time I drive it. It has the best and most detailed FFB I've ever seen, the car tells me every time of exactly what it is happening between the wheels and the actual surface. With the soft-body physics that is sort of wonderfully ruthless, realistic and true, BeamNG.drive would make the most perfect racing sim in the history in my opinion. You miss the breaking point, the tree shreds your car to pieces, race over. You cook your engine, race over.  Hit the sidewalk, wheel is fractured and suspension is bent, race over. No BS, no sugar. Exactly like in real life. 

But BeamNG.drive doesn't take itself seriously, at least not as a racing sim. It became the prime car crashing game. It has the talent of beating the siht out of _______ (insert your classy sim title here) in its own field, but it just doesn't seem to bother. Of course it provides its own distinctive sandbox driving experience that's fun and in a way is beyond a plain racing sim, just by the variety of vehicles that you can drive here. Even fully exploring a single official map would take many days I guess and it does have racing activities but it lacks racing sim features like championship mode, race series mode, leagues and so on. Maybe it would make no sense as 98% of people would probably crash each other before the first corner, I don't know. But BeamNG.drive would fit time attack type racing like rally or hillclimb so perfectly.

https://youtu.be/txY2PcuY-Rs?si=qDwu2MOiP_ifEtDo

So, for me this CAR SIM is the most honest and talented of all of them that became a crashing sim eventually. After all of these years it still says "Early access" so who knows, maybe it will include a more detailed racing module. Until that I just try to beat my times on the twisty road courses. To me it feels extremely satisfying to survive a good run in more or less one piece on a section where even rough road patches can kill you or fist-sized stones can launch the car into the air. Like in real life. By realism and difficulty, it gives the famously difficult and realistic (and great, let me add) Richard Burns Rally a run for its money in my opinion. Actually, BeamNG.drive became one of my most favourite rally experiences, ever. Drive to survive, liteRALLY.

Lovely tool to mess around with. Target audience? Perhaps those who like tools like Garry's mod but want a game with easy menu UI that can be operated with a game pad and a general theme that revolves around cars. 

Intrigued by my Summer Car but don't want any of that grind with engines and instead drive? Yes this is for you. Interested in different setups for a car model or interested in particular real life car models on how they look like / break apart as a soft physics model in the sim? This is for you. 

Lots of mods in form of tracks, car models and different setups and kits for said cars. Mod scene is weird, i see lots of passionate talk about level of quality on mods and how realistic some models look or don't look.  If none of this interests you then consider again. Quality of course varies but there is lot of the stuff. 

This game replaces nothing on the existing racing game scene, it instead occupies it's own niche slot and because of that i recommend getting it pretty openly to many but it requires at least rudimentary interest in messing around with cars and spending time checking out scenarios and mods and just spending time with the product to unlock it's potential. Devs have included some campaigns for achievements and scenarios and there is good support for wheels (Driving is nice with game pad too) but it's obvious the first requirement from the player is interest into the various topics presented in the game and spending time to find the fun parts. Nothing is served on a force fed silver plate. You choose what you want to do.

All in all a good product. Get it if you find yourself intrigued and have enough time and interest to explore.  Do not be scared of the Early Access tag. This product is very far into development at this stage (1/2024) and i have had no issues whatsoever.
